source.title: Long-range neural and gap junction protein-mediated cues control polarity during planarian regeneration.
source.location: Text, Results section 'Long-range information is provided to wounded areas...' (Figure 1B), paragraph on cuts including head region

stage: trunk fragment with pre-existing head (cut including head region)
injury: transverse amputations along the A/P axis, head region retained

intervention.timing: immediately after amputation (drug solution from amputation)
intervention.description: Octanol-exposed fragments amputated so that the original head region is retained

readout.method: external morphology and A/P axis scoring of regenerates

notes: Text: '>95% single-head (normal) animals'. Only a lower bound is given (>95%), so 95 is used as the stated bound; the complement is not reported. n not stated in text. Octanol 127 uM from Methods (Drug treatment section). Low outcome confidence because the value is a bound.

source.title: Long-range neural and gap junction protein-mediated cues control polarity during planarian regeneration.
source.location: Text, Results section 'Innexin genes ... mediate information' (Figure 3B), paragraph on intact animals

intervention.timing: dsRNA injections over about 2 weeks (five injections over 19 days), intact animals assayed about 30 days after first injection
intervention.description: Intact animals microinjected with dsRNA of Dj-Inx-5 and Dj-Inx-13 (mixed), then Dj-Inx-12 dsRNA

readout.method: markers of CNS, neoblasts and digestive system in intact animals
readout.timepoint: about 30 days after first dsRNA injection

notes: Text: 'in all cases (n=14), two new pharynxes appeared', with ectopic brain tissue and one pharynx A/P-inverted. 'other' = two ectopic pharynxes with ectopic brain in intact animals (not a bipolar head count), described per schema. duration_h computed from the 19-day injection window (456 h); timing_start_h null because the schedule is relative to first dsRNA injection, not amputation. Readout as stated in Figure 3B legend.

source.title: Long-range neural and gap junction protein-mediated cues control polarity during planarian regeneration.
source.location: Supplementary Table S1 legend (inline in fulltext, Dj-Inx-5+13,-12(RNAi) row)

intervention.timing: dsRNA injection schedule as in Figure 3A; scored in intact animals about 30 days after first injection
intervention.description: Intact animals microinjected with the innexin dsRNA mixture, subset scored for pigmentation and extra pharynxes

readout.method: scoring of pigmentation and extra pharynxes in intact animals
readout.timepoint: about 30 days after first dsRNA injection

notes: Supplementary Table S1 text: '~50%, n=30' for ectopic photoreceptor-like pigmentation and pharynxes. Converted to 15/30 (outcome_from_percent true). n_total null because only the ectopic subset is reported, which would conflict with the validator sum rule; n=30 recorded here. 'other' = ectopic photoreceptor pigmentation and extra pharynxes, described per schema. The same table reports fissioning (~43%, n=137) and lysis (~37%) for the n=137 group; these are approximate and not entered (see skipped file).

source.title: Long-range neural and gap junction protein-mediated cues control polarity during planarian regeneration.
source.location: Text, Results section 'Innexin genes ...' (Figure 3C-D), paragraph on amputated RNAi worms

intervention.timing: amputated about 25-28 days after first dsRNA injection (Figure 3C)
intervention.description: dsRNA-injected worms amputated, pharyngeal fragments scored during regeneration

readout.method: scoring of anterior and posterior structures in regenerates

notes: Text: 'bipolar head after regeneration from pharyngeal (20%, n=21)'. 20% of 21 is not an integer count (4/21=19.0%, 5/21=23.8%), so the value is stored as a percentage with outcome_from_percent true, and n_total null; n=21 is recorded here. Text describes inverted A/P axis with bipolar head (double_head).

source.title: Long-range neural and gap junction protein-mediated cues control polarity during planarian regeneration.
source.location: Figure 4A legend and text (lateral cuts, post-pharyngeal fragments)

injury: lateral transverse cuts, one or two simultaneous, disrupting ventral nerve cord

intervention.timing: immediately after amputation (drug solution from amputation)
intervention.description: Octanol-exposed post-pharyngeal fragments cut laterally (once or twice simultaneously) so as to disrupt the ventral nerve cord

readout.method: scoring of anterior structures and CNS in regenerates

'other' = anterior structures in all four blastemas (quadruple heads), described per schema. Octanol 127 uM from Methods.
